issues: scene_001: Reading the letter is a reasonable visual inference, but receiving it is the only explicitly stated action; keep the depicted reading limited to the unspecified time and place.

The summary’s statement that the fathers were about to break their covenant is explicitly anchored to the twenty-sixth year (Alma 56:7), while the young men’s taking up weapons is reported separately without a date; keep these as distinct events, as the scene notes require.
The line of narration is an exact excerpt from Alma 56:5, but omits the verse’s preceding word “Therefore”; retain it only as a standalone quotation, not as an alteration to a longer quotation.

scene_003: The character label “Lamanite warriors (Alma 56)” is not established in the provided list, and verse 10 reports their earlier killing rather than depicting it. Avoid showing that earlier action in this scene.
The scene is careful to present the prisoners’ presence in the land of Nephi as Helaman’s supposition, not a certain fact. The narration uses exact, contiguous source quotations.

The character label “Lamanites” is supported by the source; “chief captains” are described as prisoners, not individually identified characters. The visual inferences appropriately avoid staging past deaths or captures as present events.

The preceding scene’s events are not carried into this scene as a present-tense occurrence. The scenes can be read as successive passages in Helaman’s letter, though the source does not specify a visual setting for the letter.
scene_005: The cities’ possession by the Lamanites is reported background, not a present action; the scene appropriately prohibits depicting their capture.
scene_006: The divine favor and preservation are reported, not a visible appearance or event; no divine figure should be added.
scene_007: The rear attack is only a hoped-for plan and did not occur; keep it out of the visual scene.
scene_008: The Lamanites’ holding position is a reasonable inference, but the text does not specify a location or a particular holding action to depict.
scene_009: The provisions’ arrival and reinforcements are reported, but the verses do not explicitly place them at Judea; treat that location as uncertain.
scene_010: The march is a stratagem toward an intended destination, not an arrival; the group’s appearance with provisions is an inference from the feint.
scene_011: The spies’ report is summarized without supplied words; do not invent dialogue or stage an unsupported reporting scene.
scene_012: Helaman’s account frames the Lamanites’ supposed intent to kill his force as conjecture, not confirmed motive.
scene_013: The camp is stated, but the pursuers’ visibility from it is unspecified; keep them out of the image unless shown at an established distance.
scene_014: The account reports flight over the course of the day; avoid compressing separate moments into one continuous scene.
scene_015: The reason the Lamanites halted is unspecified; do not imply a motive.
scene_017: The mothers’ teaching and the young men’s lack of battle experience are reported past facts, not events to stage here; no mothers or invented teaching dialogue should appear.
scene_018: Antipus’s army’s battle and Helaman’s return are distinct actions; avoid making the scene imply they began simultaneously.
scene_019: The verse states that Antipus and leaders fell by the sword, but does not describe the precise action; depict no wounds, blood, or severed body parts.
scene_021: The surrender and subsequent counting are consecutive but distinct actions; do not collapse them into a single instant.
scene_022: “Strength of God” and “miraculous strength” are reported comparisons, not descriptions of visible supernatural effects; depict no divine appearance or invented effects.
scene_023: Sending prisoners toward Zarahemla and marching back toward Judea are distinct movements; neither arrival is stated.
